recentItems.title: Calls for Australia to join Israeli settlement trade ban
recentItems.description:
Australia's Palestinian representative is calling on the federal government to join a dozen countries including the UK, France and Canada in imposing a trade ban on settlements in the occupied West Bank. 

Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong has confirmed Australia will act further against Israel but has ruled out throwing weight behind the major sanctions.

SBS Political Correspondent Rayane Tamer has the details

recentItems.title: Israel labels UK's 'ethnic cleansing' comments as 'outrageous lies', hits back against sanctions
recentItems.description:
Israel says it ‌will close the British consulate in Jerusalem after the United Kingdom, France and Canada announced plans to ban imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank — something Australia has previously ruled out.

UK foreign minister Ed Miliband has told parliament there was "ethnic cleansing" of Palestinians in parts of the West Bank and the UK could no longer just "call out" injustice and suffering but had to act to oppose the expansion of settlements, which he said threatened the viability of a Palestinian state.

International concern is growing over rising settler violence and expansion of Israeli settlements, which most countries consider illegal under international law. Israel disputes this.

In a joint statement, ministers from 12 countries, including the UK, France, Canada, Spain and Sweden, reaffirmed support for a two-state solution and signalled tougher action on settlements.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar described Miliband's comments as "outrageous lies", announced entry bans on some British nationals and officials, and said the UK would no longer participate in a US-led Gaza coordination mission.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong has ruled out Australian support for a blanket ban on settlement imports, but has indicated further sanctions against Israel are being considered.

recentItems.title: ‘I think this is from China’: Philippine defence chief handed note on stage about South China Sea
recentItems.description:
Watch the moment Philippine defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro received a handwritten note during a public forum in Seoul on Tuesday. Teodoro said it was passed to him by someone associated with the Chinese government, denouncing it on stage as an act of “coercion, bullying and aggression”.

Teodoro was speaking at the Seoul Defense Dialogue, an annual multilateral security forum, when a man approached him during a question-and-answer session and handed him a piece of paper.

The wording, read aloud by Teodoro, closely mirrors language China’s foreign ministry has used repeatedly in official statements on the South China Sea, including a July statement marking 10 years since an international tribunal ruled against Beijing’s claims, which described Chinese actions in the waterway as “reasonable, legitimate, professional and restrained”.

Reuters could not independently verify who handed Teodoro the note or confirm that it originated from an associate of China.

The Philippines and China have clashed repeatedly over the South China Sea, where Beijing claims sovereignty over nearly the entire waterway despite a 2016 ruling by an international arbitration tribunal that found its claims had no legal basis. China does not recognise the ruling.

recentItems.title: Jon Stewart criticises former NYC officials as 9/11 records released
recentItems.description:
Comedian Jon Stewart, a long-time advocate for September 11 first responders and survivors, criticised former New York City officials for withholding information about health concerns following the 2001 attacks.

"We've lost three times as many people to 9/11-related illnesses as we did on 9/11," Stewart said alongside advocates and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

His comments came after the city announced the release of more than 170,000 pages of records documenting its response to the attacks and their aftermath. The announcement also included a settlement of two lawsuits seeking access to files related to post-9/11 health and air quality concerns.

The documents, available through a new city online portal, include records on health issues, air quality and the broader municipal response to the attacks, according to Mr Mamdani's office. They also include the so-called Harding memo, previously unlocated records known as the "68 boxes," and files concerning World Trade Center 7.

recentItems.title: Would you use 3% of your  super payments to pay for your rent or mortgage?
recentItems.description:
One Nation is proposing a policy that would allow workers to divert 3%t of their super payments straight to their wallet for three years — investing only 9% instead of the current compulsory rate of 12%.

Party leader Pauline Hanson said the policy would give households "breathing room" and would help people to buy groceries, pay power bills and cover the costs of raising a family.

But the policy has been criticised for its potential impact on retirement, with some saying it could leave thousands worse off later in life.

SBS News took to the streets to find out what people really think about One Nation's proposed super policy.

Read more: https://bit.ly/4ynhQk7
